To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the boundary concentrated finite element methods are a powerful numerical tool for the solution of elliptic boundary problems with smooth coefficients, that they are particularly well suited for parallel implementation, and that they are robust in the sense that they yield accurate approximations of the solutions of these problems without the use of mesh refinement.
we present two multigrid methods that lead to preconditioners with condition numbers that do not depend on the number of unknowns N.

the condition numbers of the preconditioned stiffness matrices of two multilevel methods for the boundary concentrated finite element discretization of elliptic boundary-value problems are uniformly bounded in the problem size, and the cost of applying the multilevel preconditioner is O(N).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of numerical methods for the solution of partial differential equations that occur in the modeling of physical and engineering problems.
the development, analysis, and implementation of numerical methods for the solution of partial differential equations that arise in applications.
the development of efficient numerical methods for elliptic boundary value and eigenvalue problems with low regularity boundary and interface conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the boundary concentrated finite element approach is a very promising method for the numerical treatment in particular of elliptic boundary valued problems with smooth coefficients, but also for other problems, e.g. with nonsmooth coefficients.
the method is a powerful and efficient tool for solving elliptic boundary value problem with smooth coefficients and boundary conditions with low regularity.
the method is not only very promising for problems with smooth data, but also for those with low regularity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have presented a new preconditioning technique for the hp-version of finite element method that has the potential to solve problems of size N with O(N) operations.

the hp-FEM can be made to work very well for elliptic problems with low regularity boundary data and coefficients, and that multilevel preconditioned iterative solvers for the hp-FEM are very efficient.
we can solve the problem with the same accuracy as the finite element discretization, with the same number of unknowns as the finite element method, but with a much better convergence rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for the hp-version of FEM, the condition number of the stiffness matrix is not necessarily the bottleneck for the convergence of Krylov subspace methods.
the boundary concentrated finite element space can be used to design efficient preconditioners.
multigrid can be applied to a wide variety of discretization methods, and that it can be very effective for solving the resulting systems of equations.
